progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: B3a part 1 and earlier: gametes, internal fertilisation, the corpus luteum, hCG and progesterone, and the placenta taking charge of progesterone. Students may have heard of periods and labour but not of FSH, LH, the pituitary or feedback.
progression.startsWith: The question left by part 1: an egg is released about once a month, so what stops another egg for nine months?
progression.stopsAfter: Explaining that progesterone returning in the blood turns FSH and LH down (negative feedback) so no new egg is released through pregnancy; that late oestrogen makes the uterus muscle more responsive to oxytocin; tracing the birth loop as positive feedback that ends when the baby is born; separating prolactin (makes milk) from oxytocin (ejects milk) and why milk is held back in pregnancy; and writing an Explain answer using both loops.
progression.nextLesson: The agriculture video: how people use what we know about reproduction (plants and animals) to change outcomes, and how to evaluate it.

teaching.task: Explain how negative and positive feedback are both used in the hormonal control of pregnancy and birth, and say which hormone makes and which moves milk.
teaching.causalExplanation: FSH and LH from the pituitary grow a follicle and release an egg, and progesterone in the blood acts back on the pituitary and turns them down, which is negative feedback. In pregnancy the source of progesterone changes from the corpus luteum to the placenta but the pituitary senses it the same way, so the brake stays on. At birth the baby's head stretches the cervix, nerve signals make the pituitary release oxytocin, the muscle contracts harder and stretches the cervix more, so the result adds to the process, which is positive feedback, until the baby is born and the stretch stops. Prolactin makes milk and oxytocin squeezes it out.
teaching.conversationalApproach: Starts from the question part 1 left open, builds each loop one arrow at a time with a persistent loop card, maps the brake onto a thermostat, shows the birth loop as a ring that gets stronger on each lap, defines negative and positive by what the result does to the process, models an Explain answer, then tests an unseen tablet case, a milk case and a feelings-based misconception.
teaching.openingDecision: What stops the next egg for nine months, why does labour only get stronger once it starts, and how does the body make milk and move it?
teaching.understandingCheck: Predict FSH, LH and ovulation for a non-pregnant woman taking a progesterone-like hormone at a pregnancy-level concentration, say whether prolactin or oxytocin is the problem when milk is made but little comes out, and correct a student who calls labour negative feedback because it is painful.
teaching.curriculumScope: Analyse the required features and hormonal control of a scoped mammalian model (Module 5): progesterone negative feedback on FSH and LH, oestrogen effect on the uterus muscle, birth as positive feedback with oxytocin, and prolactin and oxytocin in lactation. Contraception, a full hormone cycle, fetal hormone signals and the hypothalamus detail are deferred.

design.visualSystem: Explainer engine: warm paper stage, handwritten Caveat headings, amber doodle layer, part 1 tract and fetus-and-placenta plates reused with one new aligned term uterus pair, coded brain and pituitary outline, loop diagrams, a thermostat loop, a hormone graph and a milk gland schematic. Fixed hormone colours: amber progesterone, slate FSH and LH, magenta oestrogen, violet oxytocin, green prolactin, cream milk; negative loops use a flat-ended arrow and a minus, positive loops a plus.
design.transitionPlan: The tract plate stays while the brain outline slides in; the plate fades to a quiet field for the loop diagram; the loop slides up for the thermostat; the graph replaces the loop; the camera pushes into the uterus wall and then the cervix; the chain moves to the centre and closes into a ring; the two loop icons enlarge into a comparison card; the milk gland replaces the plates; the attempt board removes the loop card and it returns in the feedback; scene crossfade with settle.
